title: The DOM: selecting and changing the page
goal: Use JavaScript to find elements on a page and change their text, attributes, classes and styles.

concepts: The DOM is a tree of objects the browser builds from your HTML
Loading scripts: <script src defer> or at the end of body
querySelector and querySelectorAll with CSS selectors
textContent vs innerHTML (and why innerHTML with user input is dangerous)
classList.add/remove/toggle/contains instead of changing style directly
Attributes and dataset: getAttribute, setAttribute, data-* attributes

build.task: In day37/, build a 'profile switcher' page: an HTML card showing name, role, photo and a skills list, plus three buttons with data-person="0|1|2". In app.js, store 3 people as an array of objects. You don't have events yet (tomorrow), so for today write a function showPerson(index) that updates the card's text, image src and alt, skills list, and toggles a 'highlight' class when the person has more than 4 skills. Call showPerson(0), showPerson(1), showPerson(2) from the console to test. Also write a function countElements() that logs how many elements of each tag the page has, using querySelectorAll('*').
acceptance: Script loaded with defer (or at the end of body)
showPerson updates name, role, image src and alt, and rebuilds the skills list
Uses textContent for text (not innerHTML)
Uses classList.toggle(name, condition) for the highlight
countElements logs a correct object of tag counts

hints: Select once at the top: const nameEl = document.querySelector('.card-name'); then reuse it.
Rebuild a list: ul.textContent = ''; then for each skill create an li with document.createElement('li'), set its textContent, and ul.append(li).
classList.toggle('highlight', person.skills.length > 4) adds or removes the class based on the condition.

explainBack.q: Why does your script need defer? What happens without it in the <head>?
lookFor: script runs before HTML is parsed
defer waits until the DOM is ready

explainBack.q: Why use textContent instead of innerHTML for names coming from data?
lookFor: textContent treats it as plain text

lastHintExplanation: A script in the <head> without defer runs before the body is parsed, so querySelector finds nothing and returns null. defer waits until the HTML is parsed. textContent inserts plain text, while innerHTML parses its input as HTML, so untrusted data could inject markup or scripts (XSS).

questions.q: A is 50% more efficient than B. B takes 30 days. How long does A take?
questions.why: A's rate is 1.5 times B's, so 30 / 1.5 = 20.

questions.q: A and B together take 10 days and B alone takes 15. How long does A take alone?

4 men and 6 women finish a job in 8 days; 3 men and 7 women finish it in 10 days. How long would 10 women take?
questions.why: 8(4m + 6w) = 10(3m + 7w) gives m = 11w. The job is 8 × 50w = 400 woman-days, so 10 women need 40 days.

questions.why: The whole job takes 20 days, so the remaining 60% takes 12.

title: Events: clicks, input and forms
goal: Make pages respond to users with event listeners, and handle forms without reloading the page.

concepts: addEventListener('click' | 'input' | 'change' | 'submit' | 'keydown', handler)
The event object: target, currentTarget, key, preventDefault()
Form submit: preventDefault, reading values, FormData
Live validation on input events; showing error messages
Event bubbling: events travel up to parents
Removing listeners and avoiding inline onclick

build.task: In day38/: (1) connect yesterday's profile switcher buttons with click events; (2) build a signup form (name, email, password, confirm password, terms checkbox) with live validation on input: show a specific message under each field, a password strength meter (weak/medium/strong) and a submit button that's disabled until everything is valid. On submit, preventDefault, read values with FormData, and show a success card instead of the form. (3) Add a keyboard shortcut: pressing '/' focuses the name field.
acceptance: No inline onclick attributes; all events via addEventListener
Each field shows its own error message while typing, clearing when fixed
Password strength updates live with at least 3 levels and clear rules
Submit is disabled until all fields are valid; page never reloads on submit
Success card shows the submitted name and email
'/' focuses the name field (but not while typing in another input)

hints: One validate() function that checks everything and returns an object of errors makes life easy. Call it on every input event and on submit.

Error messages: put an empty

under each field and set its textContent.
For the '/' shortcut: document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === '/' && e.target.tagName !== 'INPUT') { e.preventDefault(); nameInput.focus(); } }).

explainBack.q: Why do you call preventDefault() in the submit handler?
lookFor: default submit sends the form and reloads/navigates
we handle it in JS instead

explainBack.q: What's the difference between e.target and e.currentTarget?
lookFor: target is the element actually clicked
currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to
differ when bubbling from a child

explainBack.q: Walk through what happens in your code from typing one character in the email field to the error message updating.

lastHintExplanation: A form's default submit action sends the data and reloads or navigates the page, so preventDefault() lets you handle it in JavaScript. e.target is the element where the event started (e.g. a span inside a button); e.currentTarget is the element whose listener is running. Events bubble from the target up through its ancestors.

predict.why: The event fires on the button, then bubbles up to the div.

title: Rendering lists from data
goal: Keep your data in an array and render the page from it, so the UI always matches the data.

concepts: Data first: the array is the source of truth, the DOM is a view of it
A render() function that rebuilds the list from data
createElement, append, and DocumentFragment for many items
Search and filter: render a filtered copy, don't delete data
Sorting controls that re-render
Empty states: what to show when there's nothing

build.task: In day39/, build a 'Course catalogue' page. Data: an array of at least 12 course objects (title, category, level, price, rating). UI: a search box (filters by title as you type), a category dropdown, a level filter (checkboxes), a sort select (price low→high, high→low, rating), and a results count ('Showing 5 of 12'). Render course cards from the filtered and sorted data with a render() function. Show a friendly empty state when nothing matches, with a 'Clear filters' button.
acceptance: All UI is rendered from the data array through one render() function
Search, category, level and sort work together (combined filters)
Original data array never changes when filtering or sorting
Results count is always correct
Empty state appears when nothing matches; Clear filters resets every control and re-renders
Search is case-insensitive

hints: Keep the filter state in one object: const state = { query: '', category: 'all', levels: [], sort: 'none' }. Each control updates state and calls render().
render(): let list = courses.filter(...).filter(...); then sort a copy; then build cards. Never touch courses itself.
Use a DocumentFragment or build an array of elements and call container.replaceChildren(...cards) for one DOM update.

explainBack.q: Explain the flow from changing the category dropdown to the cards updating.
lookFor: render() recalculates filtered list from original data

explainBack.q: Why is it better to filter a copy and re-render than to hide/remove DOM elements directly?

lastHintExplanation: With 'data first', the array plus a small state object are the truth, and render() is a function of them: it filters and sorts a copy and rebuilds the DOM. Every control just updates state and calls render(), so filters combine naturally and the UI can never drift from the data. This is the same idea Angular uses later.

predict.q: const all = [3, 1, 2]; const shown = all.sort(); console.log(all)
predict.why: sort mutates the original array and returns it.

title: Project: a to-do app
goal: Build a complete to-do app with add, complete, edit, delete and filters, using the data-first pattern.

concepts: Planning state: an array of { id, text, done, createdAt }
Unique ids: crypto.randomUUID() or Date.now()
Actions as functions: addTodo, toggleTodo, editTodo, deleteTodo
Inline editing: double-click to edit, Enter to save, Escape to cancel
Filters: all / active / completed, and 'clear completed'

resources.title: TodoMVC (see how a to-do app behaves)

build.task: Build a to-do app in day40/ (index.html, style.css, app.js). Features: add a task (Enter or button; ignore empty input), mark complete with a checkbox, edit by double-clicking the text (Enter saves, Escape cancels, empty text deletes), delete button, filter buttons All/Active/Completed with the active filter highlighted, an 'X items left' counter, and 'Clear completed'. All changes go through action functions that update the array and then call render().
acceptance: Every feature listed works, including Escape-to-cancel while editing
State is a single array of objects with unique ids; DOM is only changed in render()
Items-left counter and filters are always correct
Accessible: checkbox has a label, buttons have accessible names, works with keyboard
Styled and usable on a phone

hints: Find items by id, not array index: todos.find(t => t.id === id). Indexes change when filtering.
Put data-id on each li, and read it in handlers with e.target.closest('li').dataset.id.
For edit mode, keep let editingId = null in state. render() shows an <input> for that item instead of text, and focuses it.
proof: Commit with day40/ files. Add a short GIF or screenshots in the commit or README if you can.

explainBack.q: Walk through what happens in your code when the user ticks a checkbox.
Why did you use ids instead of array indexes to find todos?
lookFor: filtered view index doesn't match the real array

lastHintExplanation: Each action function changes the todos array and then calls render(), so the screen always reflects the data. Ids are stable while indexes shift whenever you delete or filter: index 2 in the 'Active' view may be index 5 in the real array. Stable ids prevent editing or deleting the wrong item.

predict.q: const todos = [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }]; todos.splice(0, 1); What is todos[0].id?
predict.why: Removing the first item shifts everything left, so indexes change; ids don't.

title: localStorage and event delegation
goal: Make your to-do app remember tasks after a reload, and handle events for many items with one listener.

concepts: localStorage.setItem/getItem/removeItem: strings only
Saving objects with JSON.stringify and loading with JSON.parse
Handling missing or corrupted saved data with try/catch
Event delegation: one listener on the parent, use e.target.closest()
Why delegation works for items rendered later
sessionStorage vs localStorage; what never to store (passwords, tokens)

build.task: Copy your Day 40 app into day41/. (1) Save todos and the current filter to localStorage on every change, and load them on start. Wrap loading in try/catch so corrupted data (test by setting localStorage.todos = 'oops' in the console) falls back to an empty list instead of crashing. (2) Replace per-item listeners with ONE click listener and ONE change listener on the list (event delegation). (3) Add a 'theme' toggle (light/dark) remembered in localStorage. (4) Add an export button that downloads todos as a JSON file.
acceptance: Reloading keeps todos, completion state and the active filter
Corrupted localStorage doesn't crash the app (tested and noted in a comment)
No listeners are attached to individual items; delegation on the list handles toggle, delete and edit
Theme choice survives reload
Export downloads a valid .json file of the todos

hints: Wrap storage in two helpers: save() { localStorage.setItem('todos', JSON.stringify(todos)) } and load() { try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('todos')) ?? [] } catch { return [] } }.
Delegation: list.addEventListener('click', e => { const li = e.target.closest('li'); if (!li) return; if (e.target.matches('.delete')) deleteTodo(li.dataset.id); }).

Download: const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(todos, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' }); const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob); a.download = 'todos.json'; a.click();

explainBack.q: Explain how event delegation works in your list, and why it keeps working after render() replaces all items.
lookFor: closest/matches identify the item and action
parent isn't replaced so listener survives

explainBack.q: Why must you JSON.stringify before saving to localStorage?
What should never be stored in localStorage and why?
lookFor: any script on the page can read it (XSS)

lastHintExplanation: Event delegation puts one listener on a parent that never gets replaced. Clicks on any item bubble up to it, and e.target.closest('li') identifies which item was hit, so it works for items rendered later. localStorage only stores strings: without JSON.stringify an object is saved as '[object Object]'. Any script on the page can read localStorage, so never put secrets there.

predict.why: localStorage converts every value to a string.
The object is converted with String(), which gives '[object Object]'.

dsa.note: Two-way mapping again, then a lookup-table problem.
